extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, disciplinary counsel, and USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff
extracted.subtask_description: Final Order approving an Affidavit of Resignation under 37 C.F.R. § 11.27 and imposing an exclusion on consent from practice before the USPTO, describing procedural, substantive, and reinstatement-related standards and obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to approve affidavit and exclude (jurisdictional basis)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director of the USPTO has authority to approve an Affidavit of Resignation and to exclude a practitioner on consent pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 C.F.R. § 11.27.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order invokes these statutes and regulations as the legal basis for accepting the affidavit and ordering exclusion on consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of USPTO professional responsibility rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A registered patent practitioner is subject to the USPTO Code of Professional Responsibility and Disciplinary Rules (see 37 C.F.R. § 11.19(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary proceedings and standards apply to registered practitioners under these rules; conduct is evaluated under the cited regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit of Resignation substantive requirements (37 C.F.R. § 11.27(a) acknowledgements)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Resignation Affidavit must include the practitioner's acknowledgements that: (1) consent is freely and voluntarily rendered and not the result of coercion or duress and that the practitioner is fully aware of the implications; (2) the practitioner is the subject of a pending investigation concerning conduct in connection with practice before the Office and the affidavit identifies the allegations; (3) the practitioner is aware the OED Director is of the opinion that the conduct may have violated identified rules (as applicable); (4) the practitioner is aware that if he/she applies for reinstatement under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 the OED Director will conclusively presume, for purposes of reinstatement, that the facts underlying the investigation are true and that the practitioner could not have successfully defended against the allegations; (5) the practitioner is aware of the implications of resignation (i.e., exclusion from practice before the Office); and (6) the practitioner desires to be excluded from practice before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order treats these numbered acknowledgements (points 1–6) as satisfying the requirements of § 11.27(a). The affidavit should explicitly state these acknowledgements to be approved for exclusion on consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proscribed conduct: accepting compensation from third party without client consent (37 C.F.R. § 10.68(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 C.F.R. § 10.68(a)(1) proscribes accepting compensation from one other than the practitioner's client for legal services without obtaining the client's consent after full disclosure to the client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order cites the OED Director's opinion that Respondent's conduct may have violated § 10.68(a)(1). The decision describes anti-patterns illustrating the rule: fee payments handled through a third-party entity (PTI/IPA), failure to disclose the agreement to customers, directing USPTO correspondence to the third party's address, failing to communicate directly with the inventor-clients, and third-party control of payment from purported escrow accounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumptions on reinstatement applications (37 C.F.R. § 11.60)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a practitioner applies for reinstatement under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 after exclusion on consent, the OED Director will conclusively presume, for the limited purpose of determining reinstatement, that (i) the facts upon which the investigation is based are true and (ii) the practitioner could not have successfully defended himself against the allegations in the investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants for reinstatement should be aware that the Director will treat the underlying investigative facts as conclusively established for reinstatement proceedings; this is an explicit consequence described in the affidavit and Final Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligations during exclusion (37 C.F.R. § 11.58 compliance)
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner excluded on consent must 'comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58' while excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the Order does not recite § 11.58 text, it imposes full compliance with that regulation as an express condition of the exclusion; practitioners should consult § 11.58 for the specific duties (e.g., notice and transitional responsibilities) required while excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notice of final order (OED Reading Room and Official Gazette)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish the Final Order at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's Reading Room and shall publish a Notice of Exclusion on Consent in the Official Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order sets out the exact publication locations and includes a model Notice of Exclusion on Consent that summarizes the facts and the basis for the exclusion; publication is a required procedural step following approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to disciplinary agencies, courts, and public (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59, the OED Director shall give notice of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the State(s) where the practitioner is admitted, to courts where the practitioner is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order directs the OED Director to carry out these notification obligations as part of the disciplinary process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of exclusion (practice restrictions)
rubrics_metrics.description: The practitioner is excluded on consent from the practice of patent, trademark, and other non-patent law before the Office effective on the date of the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order specifies the domains of practice from which the practitioner is excluded; practitioners and counsel should note the exclusion's coverage before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and the Respondent shall bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of the agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order expressly provides that each side bears its own costs; this is a term of the consent exclusion.
